title: StackTeck, Churchill Container Honored by IMDA for Applications Utilizing PureFive® Resin
summary: PureCycle Technologies announced today that two different products made with its PureFive® resin were recognized among the winners of the 2026 (IMDA) Awards Competition.
body_markdown:
**ORLANDO, Fla. – September 23, 2026, —**[PureCycle Technologies, Inc.](https://www.purecycle.com/) (Nasdaq: PCT) announced today that two different products made with its PureFive® resin were recognized among the winners of the 2026 In-Mold Decorating Association (IMDA) Awards Competition. StackTeck Systems earned an Honorable Mention in the Sustainable Use of In-Mold Processes – Design Achievement category for its 6 oz. IML TRIM Cup, and Churchill Container took home the win for Best Use in a Packaging Application of a Prototype Product or In-House Promotion with its “Rockstar Cup.” Both products are made using PureCycle's recycled polypropylene that is suitable for food contact.


The IMDA Awards recognize the year's top applications in in-mold labeling, in-mold decorating and in-mold electronics. This year's winners were revealed at the Plastic Product Decorating Summit, held September 2 in Sugar Land, Texas, with entries judged on design and complexity, integration of the in-mold element, functionality, and innovation in materials and process.


StackTeck's 6 oz. IML TRIM Cup combines the company's Thin Recess Injection Molding (TRIM) technology with 30% PureFive® resin, using ultra-thin panels that cut part weight by 20% compared to conventional designs. The cup is decorated with MCC Verstraete's Ultra Gloss/Matt IML labels and is fully recyclable, pairing a lighter-weight package with the high-impact graphics brand owners look for on shelf.


“We are very pleased to have the recognition that this IMDA Award brings. We also want to highlight the importance of successfully molding food-grade PCR resin in an ultra-lightweight cup,” said Jordan Robertson, StackTeck Vice President of Business Development and Marketing. “We were very satisfied with the results using PureCycle material while molding a part with thin panels having a thickness of only 0.010 inches (including the 0.0024 inch thickness of the label) to produce top quality packaging with attractive IML graphics. Many thanks to PureCycle and MCC Verstraete for providing the resin and IML labels for this application.”


Churchill Container's Rockstar Cup, meanwhile, was built to showcase what durable, cold-foil IML decoration can do for reusable drinkware. The cup pairs long-lasting visual decoration with 100% recycled polypropylene and an invisible, scannable code that supports reuse tracking without disrupting the design. While the “Rockstar Cup” began as a limited demonstration series, the concept has already found its way into commercial production programs.


"We’re honored to receive this award with PureCycle and iPB printing,” said Erik Johnson, Churchill Container Program Director. “The Run It Back™ cup is designed for reuse and delivers proof that recycling works directly into the hands of consumers. The fact that it has already found its way into large scale national events is a testament to the importance of never giving up and believing in ideas that can change the world."


PureCycle Director of Sustainability and External Affairs Christian Bruey said, "Seeing PureFive® resin at the center of two award-winning applications in the same competition is a strong signal for where sustainable packaging is headed. StackTeck and Churchill Container each pushed their own technology further while proving that recycled polypropylene can meet the design, performance and shelf-appeal standards brand owners expect. We're proud to help make that possible."


Both the 6 oz IML TRIM Cup and the Rockstar Cup add to a growing list of award-winning packaging built on PureCycle's PureFive® resin, as brand owners and converters continue to look for recycled materials that don't require a trade-off between sustainability and performance.

**About PureCycle Technologies**


PureCycle Technologies LLC., a subsidiary of PureCycle Technologies, Inc., holds a global license for the only patented dissolution recycling technology, developed by The Procter & Gamble Company (P&G), that is designed to transform polypropylene plastic waste (designated as #5 plastic) into a continuously renewable resource. The unique purification process removes color, odor, and other impurities from #5 plastic waste resulting in our PureFive® resin that can be recycled and reused multiple times, changing our relationship with plastic.[www.purecycle.com](https://www.purecycle.com/)
